name: Eco-Metropolis (Innovisionaries)
tagline: A three-level city-building game that teaches sustainability, ending with urban-planning decisions made on real NASA Earth data.
problem: Sustainability is hard to teach as a lesson; students need to practise the trade-offs cities face.
solution: A Pygame city-building simulation with levels for ages 12–14, 14–16 and 16–18: guided basics, then resource and waste decisions, then data-driven planning with NASA Worldview/MODIS and UAE government datasets scored on carbon, water and biodiversity. Players take roles such as urban planner or waste manager.

why_it_stood_out.claim: Won the award for the project that captures our hearts.
Inspires sustainability through gameplay: players make urban planning and resource decisions based on real-world environmental data.
Levels are matched to school age groups, so one game spans a curriculum.
The challenge asked for a lesson plan; turning it into a playable game made the entry memorable to judges.

lessons: A familiar game genre can carry an education challenge further than the literal deliverable.
No AI in the product and a prototype on a shared drive still won an inspiration award.

sources.note: Team-written game design, levels, data list; AI use 'N/A'.
